```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

gristmillr reads and writes [Grist](https://www.getgrist.com/) documents
through the REST API. Functions take a document handle first, take and return
data frames, and work in pipelines. The examples need a Grist account, so
they are not run here.

## Authenticate

gristmillr needs an API key, which you can create in Grist under *Profile
settings*. The simplest setup is two environment variables in your
`.Renviron` (see `usethis::edit_r_environ()`):

```
GRIST_API_KEY=<your key>
GRIST_SERVER=https://myteam.getgrist.com
```

`GRIST_SERVER` defaults to `https://docs.getgrist.com`. For a self-hosted
site, include the team path if needed, e.g. `http://localhost:8484/o/docs`.

You can also pass the key directly, as a string or as a function that looks it
up each time (handy with a keyring):

```{r}
library(gristmillr)

doc <- grist_doc("<doc id>", api_key = \() keyring::key_get("grist"))
```

A key given as a string is held in memory for the session and is never saved
with the object, so saving a handle with `saveRDS()` or in a targets pipeline
doesn't write your key to disk. Use the function form for handles you persist.

## Find a document

`grist_doc()` accepts a document ID or the URL of a document, and the handle
remembers the server:

```{r}
doc <- grist_doc("https://myteam.getgrist.com/doc/<doc id>")
doc
```

If you don't know the ID, list what you can see:

```{r}
grist_orgs()
grist_workspaces("current")
grist_docs("current")

grist_doc_info(doc)
```

You can also create documents with `grist_doc_create()`, which returns a
handle.

## Read data

```{r}
grist_tables(doc)
grist_columns(doc, "People")

grist_records(doc, "People")
```

Filter and sort on the server, and limit the number of rows:

```{r}
doc |>
  grist_records(
    "People",
    filter = list(status = c("active", "pending")),
    sort = "-age",
    limit = 100
  )
```

For anything more involved, run SQL (`SELECT` only):

```{r}
grist_sql(doc, "SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM People GROUP BY status")
grist_count(doc, "People")
```

### Column types

The `convert` argument controls how Grist cell values become R vectors:

* `"auto"` (the default) reads the table's column types, so `Int` becomes
  integer, `Date` becomes `Date`, `DateTime` becomes `POSIXct`, and
  `ChoiceList` and `RefList` become list-columns. It costs one extra request
  per call.
* `"basic"` simplifies the JSON without looking up column types. Dates stay as
  numbers (seconds since 1970).
* `"raw"` returns the API's values unchanged.

`Ref` columns hold the row `id` of a record in another table. See
`vignette("joining-tables")` for resolving and joining them.

## Write data

Writes take a data frame and are converted the same way:

```{r}
new <- data.frame(name = c("Ann", "Bob"), age = c(31L, 45L))
ids <- grist_records_add(doc, "People", new)

# Returns the new row IDs. Updates need an `id` column
grist_records_update(doc, "People", data.frame(id = ids[[1]], age = 32L))

grist_records_delete(doc, "People", ids)
```

To match on a column rather than the row `id`, use `grist_records_upsert()`.
It updates records whose `by` values match and adds the rest, and never
deletes anything. `mode = "update"` or `"insert"` limits it to one of the two,
and `onmany` says what to do if several records match one row.

```{r}
latest <- data.frame(name = c("Ann", "Cy"), age = c(32L, 28L))
grist_records_upsert(doc, "People", latest, by = "name")
```

Large writes are sent in chunks. With `convert = "auto"`, a column that doesn't
exist in the table is an error, so typos surface before anything is sent.

## Change the schema

```{r}
grist_table_create(doc, "Pets", c(name = "Text", age = "Int"))

grist_columns_add(doc, "Pets", c(owner = "Ref:People", adopted = "Date"))
grist_columns_modify(doc, "Pets", data.frame(id = "age", description = "In years"))
```

## Settings

Rarely changed settings live in small option objects, so function signatures
stay short:

```{r}
doc <- grist_doc("<doc id>", options = grist_request_options(timeout = 60))

grist_records(doc, "People", options = grist_read_options(col_names = "label"))
grist_records_add(doc, "People", new, options = grist_write_options(chunk_size = 100))
```

Set defaults for a whole session with
`options(gristmillr.request_options = ..., gristmillr.read_options = ...,
gristmillr.write_options = ...)`.

## Deleting safely

Functions that delete things, such as `grist_doc_delete()` and
`grist_workspace_delete()`, take `mode = "trash"` (the default, recoverable) or
`"permanent"`. In an interactive session they ask for confirmation. In a
script they refuse to run unless you pass `confirm = TRUE`.

```{r}
doc |> grist_doc_delete()
doc |> grist_doc_restore()
```

## Other features

* Download documents or tables with `grist_doc_download()`.
* Manage attachments with `grist_attachments*()` and webhooks with
  `grist_webhook*()`.
* Review changes with `grist_doc_history()`, `grist_snapshots()` and
  `grist_doc_compare()`.

For an endpoint gristmillr doesn't wrap, `grist_request()` returns an
authenticated httr2 request:

```{r}
grist_request(doc, "tables") |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_json()
```
